resources.string: Grab the screen from anywhere, crop it, and share it. Nothing is saved to your device.

Choose Circle to Share as the digital assistant app (Default digital assistant app > Circle to Share). This makes the assistant gesture open the crop overlay (e.g., press and hold the power button, or swipe up from a bottom corner). If a \"Use screen data\" toggle is shown there, enable it.

If your device doesn\'t hand screenshots to third-party assistants, the accessibility service captures the screen instead. Under Accessibility > Circle to Share, turn on the main \"Use\" toggle. (This also powers the Quick Settings tile and the floating button below.)
Tap Open assistant settings, then Default digital assistant app. Choose \"Circle to Share\". If present, turn \"Use screen data\" or \"Use screenshot\" on.

Tap Open accessibility settings and agree. Open \"Circle to Share\" (under Downloaded apps), turn on \"Use Circle to Share\", and tap Allow. Toggle greyed out (\"Restricted setting\")? Open App info for \"Circle to Share\", tap ⋮ at the top, choose \"Allow restricted settings\", then try again.

Needs the capture fallback (step 2) on. Then tap Add Quick Settings tile if you have it, or add the tile by hand: pull down the shade twice, tap the edit (pencil) button, find \"Circle to Share\" and drag it up into your tiles.
Menus on your phone may look different.
Invoke your assistant (hold the power button, or swipe up from a bottom corner), circle what you want, then hit Share. Tip: the test button below captures this screen.
• Power button (assistant-powered): press and hold. Set under System > Gestures > Press & hold power button > Digital assistant, if it opens the power menu instead.
• Corner swipe (assistant-powered): swipe up from a bottom corner. A different way to invoke the assistant, if enabled in your system settings.

• Quick Settings tile: tapping closes the shade and captures the screen behind it. To add it, pull down the shade, tap the edit button, and drag the \"Circle to Share\" tile into your tiles. Needs the accessibility fallback (step 2) enabled.
• Floating button (below): the app\'s own always-on-screen bubble you can tap and drag. Needs the accessibility fallback (step 2) enabled.
Press and hold the power button
Hold the power button for about a second: the crop tool opens. Needs step 1. If the power menu opens instead, set System > Gestures > Press & hold power button to Digital assistant.
Swipe up from a bottom corner
Swipe diagonally up and inward from either bottom corner. Needs step 1 and gesture navigation with \"Swipe to invoke assistant\" on (System > Gestures > System navigation).
Capture with the Quick Settings tile
Pull down the shade and tap \"Circle to Share\": the shade closes and the screen behind it is captured. Needs step 2 and the tile added (see Add Quick Settings tile).
Turn on Show floating capture button below, then tap the bubble from any app. Drag it out of the way; long-press it to open this app. Needs step 2.
The tile is already in your Quick Settings.
Couldn\'t open the add-tile prompt. Add it from the shade\'s edit screen instead.
Unlock the device first to capture the screen.
The device was still unlocking. Call the assistant again to capture the screen.
A small draggable bubble on screen. Tap it to capture, crop, and share from anywhere; long-press to open this app.
Capture the screen to crop and share
Tap to restore your last crop
Draw a freeform loop around what you want and its outline becomes the crop box. Turn off to drag a rectangle directly.
Crop edges snap to the buttons, cards, and images that were on screen. Element positions are read at the moment of capture and not stored. Needs the accessibility fallback (step 2).
Highlights QR codes found in the capture. Tap it to copy its content or open its link. Scanning happens locally on this device.
Not a color. Use a hex code like #FFCA28
Couldn\'t get a screenshot. Enable the fallback in the Circle to Share app, or turn on \"Use screen data\" in assistant settings.
Couldn\'t save the image. Is the device\'s storage full?
Set Circle to Share as your assistant app first.
Couldn\'t open settings on this device.
Open Circle to Share and agree to the accessibility disclosure first.
Before you turn on the accessibility service

Circle to Share uses Android\'s Accessibility API (AccessibilityService) to capture your screen when you ask it to: from the Quick Settings tile, the floating button, or as a fallback for the assistant gesture. It is not an accessibility tool. Nothing it accesses is collected by, sent to, or shared with the developer or anyone else.

• A screenshot of your screen at the moment you trigger a capture.

• The positions and sizes of the elements on screen (not their text or content) at that same moment, and only while "Snap to screen content" is switched on.

• Notices from the system that a window has opened or changed, with the window's title and the app it belongs to, and the positions of system windows to recognize the lock screen, the power menu and the notification shade, so the floating button and the crop tool get out of their way.

• Everything is processed on this device, in memory, to show you the crop tool.

• The part you share or copy is written to the app's private cache so the receiving app can read it. Files older than an hour are deleted the next time you capture.

• An image leaves Circle to Share only when you tap Share or Copy, and only to the app you choose. The app has no internet permission.

• The service never taps, types or changes settings for you. Its only action is closing the notification shade when you use the Quick Settings tile.

Tap Agree to allow this. You then switch the service on in Android\'s accessibility settings, and can switch it off there at any time.\n\nTap No thanks to keep using Circle to Share with the assistant gesture only. The tile, the floating button and snapping stay off, and a service that is already on is switched off.
Circle to Share is free. If you like it, you can support its development with a small, voluntary donation. It unlocks nothing.

Lets Circle to Share capture the screen when you trigger it with the assistant gesture, the Quick Settings tile, or the app\'s floating button. You can then crop and share it. Screen content (element positions) is read only at the moment of capture, and only to align the crop box with what\'s on screen; if enabled in the app. Nothing is captured until you trigger it, nothing is saved to your device, and nothing ever leaves it.
